contentBlocks.text: You learned 'sh' makes one sound last week. Today, another digraph: 'ch'!

When C and H sit together, they blend into one new sound: 'ch', like at the start of 'chip' or the end of 'much'. Practice reading these words with 'ch': chip, chat, much, such. Just like 'sh' last week, notice 'ch' can appear at the start (chip, chat) or the end (much, such) of a word.
You now know two digraphs — sh and ch! Tomorrow we'll meet something a little different: a consonant blend.

objectives: Recognize that 'ch' blends into one new sound
Blend and read words with 'ch' in starting and ending positions
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review 'sh' from last week and short O from yesterday.
2. Introduce 'ch' using the chip/much example.
3. Blend chip, chat, much, and such together.
4. Move to the worksheet: read, trace, and write each word.
5. Close by comparing 'sh' and 'ch' — both are two letters making one new sound.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the starting-position words (chip, chat) before adding the ending-position ones
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more real word with 'ch'
Explicitly connecting back to 'sh' as the same KIND of pattern (digraph) helps generalize the skill, not just memorize one example
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading, tracing, and writing activity — check that the child understands 'ch' as one blended sound and can read all four words.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly extends last week's digraph work (sh) to a second digraph (ch), reinforcing the general digraph pattern rather than treating 'sh' as a one-off exception.

generationData.instructions: Read each word by blending its sounds (remember: ch is ONE sound), trace it, then write it once more on your own.
